text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Government officials and citizens send president Franjo Tudjman their best wishes for his speedy recovery.
- Croatia marked the fifth anniversary of the Vukovar tragedy.
- Commentary: the implementation of the bankruptcy law may be postponed again so as not to force too many of Croatia's over 15,000 insolvent firms into liquidation.
- Croatia Airlines will decide by the end of the year whether it will buy Boeing or Airbus planes to renew its fleet, the company director Matija Katicic said.
- European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) granted a 20 million German marks loan to Dalmatinska banka d.d. for financing small and medium-sized entreprises.
- Croatia, Bosnia, Slovenia and Macedonia threatened federal Yugoslavia they would suspend all talks on inheritance unless it agrees to split former joint gold reserves.
- Young Herzegovinian tycoon Luka Rajic will buy Boeing 737-200 for his private carrier firm "Air Exclusive" to become competitive with Croatia Airlines, unofficial sources say.
- Jobless are on the rise not for a lack of work but because, according to Labour Ministry officials, the economy is simply incapable of using its workforce. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
